assumptions.condition: Under policy \(j\in J\) and stratum \(S=s\), the structural action is \(A=A_{c_j(s)}\).
Under policy \(j\in J\) and stratum \(S=s\), the structural outcome is \(Y=Y_{c_j(s)}\).
For every unit and configurations \(c=(r,q)\), \(c'=(r',q')\) in \(\mathcal C\), \(r=Z\) and \(r'\neq Z\) imply \(Y_c\ge Y_{c'}\).
For every unit, \(r=Z\) and \(q\le q'\) imply \(Y_{(r,q)}\le Y_{(r,q')}\).
For every unit, \(r\neq Z\) and \(q\le q'\) imply \(Y_{(r,q)}\ge Y_{(r,q')}\).
\(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(p\in\mathfrak O\).

definitions.name: Selective-Label Counterfactual-Correctness response-type class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}=\{t=(s,z,(a_c),(y_c))\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{raw}}: y_{(z,q)}\ge y_{(1-z,q')}\ \forall q,q'\in\mathcal Q;\ y_{(z,q)}\le y_{(z,q')}\ \forall q\le q';\ y_{(1-z,q)}\ge y_{(1-z,q')}\ \forall q\le q';\ y_{(r_{\mathrm{neu}},q)}=y_{(r_{\mathrm{neu}},q')}\ \forall q,q'\in\mathcal Q\}\).

definitions.name: Finite randomized selective-label SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}=\{M: M\text{ has finite }\mathcal S,J,\mathcal Q,\text{ binary }Z,A,Y,\text{ and satisfies the randomized assignment, known arm-law, common-action, common-outcome, reveal-action, masked-truth, correctness, performance-order, and neutral-invariance conditions}\}\).

definitions.name: Selective-label observable-law map
definitions.construction: For \(o=(j,s,a,y,\ell)\in\mathcal O\) and \(t=(s_t,z_t,(a_c(t)),(y_c(t)))\), set \(B_{o,t}=\rho_j\mathbf 1\{s_t=s,\ a_{c_j(s)}(t)=a,\ y_{c_j(s)}(t)=y,\ \ell=z_t\text{ if }a=1,\ \ell=\star\text{ if }a=0\}\).

definitions.name: Ground-truth-blind comparison programs
definitions.construction: Apply \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\) to every observable cell and solve the same two programs with \(B_{\mathrm{blind}}=K_{\mathrm{blind}}B\) and right-hand side \(p_{\mathrm{blind}}=K_{\mathrm{blind}}p\).

definitions.name: Finite-sample whole-set confidence construction
definitions.construction: Compute the Bonferroni simultaneous Clopper--Pearson box \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and intersect it with \(\mathfrak O\). When the intersection is nonempty, optimize \(h_e^{\top}v\) over \(v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) subject to \(Bv\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\); when it is empty, return the total fallback interval \([0,1]\).

definitions.name: Euclidean-projection plug-in endpoint estimator
definitions.construction: Project \(\widehat p\) onto \(\mathfrak O\) in Euclidean norm and evaluate both endpoint programs: \(\widehat\theta=\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\widehat p)\).

definitions.name: Projection-composed endpoint directional map
definitions.construction:
For a direction \(g\), put \(z=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).  Using the full unnormalized dual faces, define
\[
\Gamma'_p(g)=\left(
\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z,
\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z
\right).
\]
Only the slope coordinate acts on \(z\); no normalized representative is selected.

definitions.name: Active-cone and dual-face subsampling handle
definitions.construction:
At a fixed \(p\in\mathfrak O\), write \((D_L,D_U)=\Gamma'_p\) and refine the active projection cones and the extreme slopes of \(\Lambda_L(p)\) and \(\Lambda_U(p)\) by all zero and comparison hyperplanes.  Let \(\mathcal R_p\) be the resulting finite pool of nonzero restrictions to \(V_p\), and let \(\mathcal A_p\) contain every matrix obtained by stacking any ordered subset of \(\mathcal R_p\cup(-\mathcal R_p)\), without repeated rows.  For \(M\in\mathcal A_p\), set \(\Omega_M=M\Sigma_pM^{\top}\) and \(r_M=\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_M)\), and use the fixed-law constant
\[
C(p)=\max\left\{0,\max_{M\in\mathcal A_p:r_M>0}(42r_M^{1/4}+16)
\sum_{o\in\mathcal O}p_o\|\Omega_M^{\dagger/2}M(\mathbf e_o-p)\|_2^3\right\}.
\]
Use \(m_n=\max\{1,\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\}\), \(\eta_n=\min\{\alpha/2,n^{-1/12}\}\), and the lower conditional quantile \(c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}\).  In \(\mathfrak O^{32}\), test the simultaneous projection and endpoint tie at
\[
p_\dagger=\tfrac12(B^{32}_{\cdot,3}+B^{32}_{\cdot,5})
=\tfrac14(\mathbf e_2+\mathbf e_3+2\mathbf e_7).
\]
Every proposed tangent projection must be certified by a nonnegative tangent representation, all thirty-two polar inequalities, and orthogonality; every endpoint derivative must have matching feasible type-weight and all-column dual certificates before it is used in the Gaussian atomic-tie conclusion.

definitions.name: Strictly positive four-coordinate witness mixture
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\), set \(\varepsilon_{32}=\pi_4/24\), \(a_{32}=\pi_2-\pi_4/8\), and \(b_{32}=\pi_1+\pi_2-\pi_4/8\). Assign weight \(\varepsilon_{32}\) to every table row except rows \(20\) and \(32\), assign \(a_{32}\) to row \(20\), and assign \(b_{32}\) to row \(32\). The induced full and blind laws are \(B^{32}w^{32}(\pi)\) and \(K^{32}B^{32}w^{32}(\pi)\).

definitions.name: Full and blind-embedded endpoint dual faces
definitions.construction:
With the simplex mass multiplier left explicit, define
\[
\mathcal D_L=\{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{|\mathcal O|}:\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\lambda\leq h_e\},
\qquad
\mathcal D_U=\{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{|\mathcal O|}:\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\lambda\geq h_e\}.
\]
For \(p\in\mathfrak O\), define the unnormalized full optimal faces
\[
\Lambda_L(p)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_L}
\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\},
\qquad
\Lambda_U(p)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_U}
\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\}.
\]
Finally, writing \(d_K\) for the number of rows of \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\), define the embedded blind-dual subspace
\[
\mathcal E_K=\{(\alpha,K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu):
\alpha\in\mathbb R,\ \mu\in\mathbb R^{d_K}\}.
\]

definitions.name: Primitive bracket-stratum design condition
definitions.construction:
The primitive bracket-stratum condition \(\mathsf{Bracket}_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) holds when there are \(s_*\in\mathcal S\) and \(q_\ell<q_m<q_h\) in \(\mathcal Q\) such that
\[
c_e(s_*)=(1,q_m),\qquad
c_j(s_*)\in\{(1,q_\ell),(1,q_h)\}\quad(j\in J_0),
\]
at least one trial arm uses \((1,q_\ell)\), at least one trial arm uses \((1,q_h)\), and \(\rho_j>0\) for every \(j\in J_0\).  No restriction is placed on other strata, on configurations away from \(s_*\), or on additional elements of \(\mathcal Q\).

statements.statement: The observable--target image of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) is exactly \(\{(Bw,h_e^{\top}w):w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}\). In the forward direction, every \(M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) induces its distribution over legal deterministic response types. In the converse direction, every \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) canonically defines an attaining SCM \(M_w\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) by drawing \(t\sim w\), independently drawing \(D\sim\rho\), and reading the structural responses from \(t\).
statements.justification: The converse is the substantive bridge from every feasible latent optimizer to a legally realized human--AI SCM.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024, Proposition 1 and Theorem 1, give the general discrete response-function construction; this theorem identifies the exact quotient required by action-dependent truth revelation and the ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026 common \(q\)-indexed order restrictions.
statements.consumer: It licenses sharp evaluation of an untrialed PSA or assisted-decision policy without treating an algebraic completion as a causal model.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\), and define the finite random response type
\[
T=\bigl(S,Z,(A_c)_{c\in\mathcal C},(Y_c)_{c\in\mathcal C}\bigr),
\qquad
w_t=\Pr_M(T=t).
\]
The counterfactual-correctness, correct-performance-order, incorrect-performance-order, and neutral-performance-invariance assumptions are exactly the four restrictions in \(\text{def:legal-response-types}\).  Hence \(T\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) almost surely.  Therefore \(w_t\geq0\) for every legal type and \(\sum_t w_t=1\), so \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) by \(\text{def:response-simplex}\).

Fix an observable cell \(o=(j,s,a,y,\ell)\in\mathcal O\).  Randomized policy assignment and the known arm law give
\[
\Pr_M(D=j,T=t)=\Pr_M(D=j)\Pr_M(T=t)=\rho_jw_t.
\tag{1}
\]
Conditional on \(D=j\) and \(T=t\), the common-action and common-outcome assumptions give, on \(S=s\),
\[
A=a_{c_j(s)}(t),
\qquad
Y=y_{c_j(s)}(t).
\tag{2}
\]
The reveal-action and masked-truth assumptions further give \(\ell=z_t\) when \(a=1\) and \(\ell=\star\) when \(a=0\).  Partitioning by the finite values of \(T\), and then using (1), (2), and \(\text{def:selective-label-incidence-map}\), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Pr_M(O_i=o)
&=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}}
 \rho_jw_t\mathbf 1\!\left\{s_t=s,\ a_{c_j(s)}(t)=a,\ y_{c_j(s)}(t)=y,
 \ \ell=z_t\text{ if }a=1,\ \ell=\star\text{ if }a=0\right\}\\
&=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}}B_{o,t}w_t.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
Thus the observable law is \(p=Bw\).  Under intervention to policy \(e\), the common-outcome response gives the causal target
\[
\tau_e(M)=\mathbb E_M[Y_{c_e(S)}]
=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}}w_t y_{c_e(s_t)}(t)
=h_e^{\top}w.
\tag{4}
\]
This proves the forward inclusion.

Conversely, fix \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  On a finite probability space draw \(T=t\) with probability \(w_t\), independently draw \(D=j\) with probability \(\rho_j\), and define \(S,Z,(A_c),(Y_c)\) by the coordinates of \(T\).  Under policy \(j\), set
\[
A=A_{c_j(S)},
\qquad
Y=Y_{c_j(S)},
\qquad
R=A,
\]
and set \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=Z\) on \(R=1\) and \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) on \(R=0\).  Independence of the two draws proves randomized assignment, and the marginal law of \(D\) proves the known arm law.  The displayed structural equations prove both common-response assumptions, reveal-action, and masking.  Every type receiving positive mass belongs to \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\), so the four unit-level outcome restrictions hold pointwise.  Therefore the constructed model \(M_w\) belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  Repeating (3)--(4) gives observable law \(Bw\) and causal target \(h_e^{\top}w\).  This proves the converse inclusion and hence the claimed equality of observable--target images.

statements.statement: As a corollary of \(\text{thm:finite-response-converse}\), for every \(p\in\mathfrak O\) the identified set of \(\tau_e\) is \([L(p),U(p)]\); compactness attains both endpoints and mixtures of endpoint SCMs attain every intermediate value.
statements.justification: This corollary records the causal interpretation of the two programs without treating LP compactness as the novelty kernel.
statements.gap: The generic optimization implication is informed by DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024; the application-specific advance is carried by the complete strict-refinement certificate.
statements.consumer: It converts each reported LP interval into the exact set of deployment means compatible with the model.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\) and define its latent fiber
\[
F(p)=\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:Bv=p\}.
\]
It is nonempty because \(p\in B\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\), convex because its constraints are linear, and compact because it is a closed subset of the finite-dimensional compact simplex.  By \(\text{thm:finite-response-converse}\), the compatible causal values are exactly
\[
\{\tau_e(M):M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}},\ P_M(O_i)=p\}
=\{h_e^{\top}v:v\in F(p)\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The continuous linear image on the right of (1) is a nonempty compact convex subset of \(\mathbb R\), hence a compact interval.  Its attained minimum and maximum are \(L(p)\) and \(U(p)\) by \(\text{def:sharp-endpoint-programs}\).

To verify that no value between the endpoints is omitted, choose minimizer \(v_L\) and maximizer \(v_U\).  For \(0\leq\gamma\leq1\),
\[
v_\gamma=(1-\gamma)v_L+\gamma v_U\in F(p),
\qquad
h_e^{\top}v_\gamma=(1-\gamma)L(p)+\gamma U(p).
\]
The converse construction in \(\text{thm:finite-response-converse}\) produces a legal SCM for every \(v_\gamma\).  Thus the causal identified set is exactly \([L(p),U(p)]\), both endpoints are attained, and every intermediate value is attained.

statements.statement: For every \(p\in\mathfrak O\), feasibility under \(Bv=p\) implies feasibility under \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}Bv=K_{\mathrm{blind}}p\), hence \([L(p),U(p)]\subseteq[L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p),U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)]\).
statements.justification: The one-line coarsening fact fixes the direction of comparison used by the strict certificate.
statements.gap: This is a data-processing lemma, not a claim to extend LakkarajuKleinbergLeskovecLudwigMullainathan2017.
statements.consumer: It makes any strict endpoint gap interpretable as information supplied by selectively revealed labels.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(p\in\mathfrak O\), define
\[
F(p)=\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:Bv=p\},
\qquad
F_b(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
=\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:K_{\mathrm{blind}}Bv=K_{\mathrm{blind}}p\}.
\]
If \(v\in F(p)\), applying the linear map \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\) to \(Bv=p\) proves \(v\in F_b(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)\).  Thus
\[
F(p)\subseteq F_b(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p).
\tag{1}
\]
Minimization of \(h_e^{\top}v\) over the larger set in (1) cannot increase its value, and maximization over that set cannot decrease its value.  By \(\text{def:z-blind-projection}\),
\[
L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)\leq L(p)
\leq U(p)\leq U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p),
\]
which is equivalent to the asserted interval inclusion.

statements.statement: Under \(\text{def:32-design-specialization}\), all thirty-two rows of \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\) are distinct members of \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\). When \(z=0\), the neutral outcomes are constant at one and the \(r=1\) outcomes are nonincreasing; when \(z=1\), the neutral outcomes are constant at zero and the \(r=1\) outcomes are nondecreasing, so correctness, both performance orders, and neutrality hold row by row. Under the specialization, \(B^{32}\) reads only the action and outcome coordinates at the two trialed configurations \((1,q_{\ell})\) and \((1,q_h)\), together with the label when an endpoint action reveals it, whereas \(h^{32}\) reads only \(Y_{(1,q_m)}\). Thus \(A_{(1,q_m)}\) is free in the observable--target quotient even though the untrialed policy uses it to define deployment action: \(e_{32}\) is absent from the trial incidence map, and the target is outcome-only. Every action coordinate at any other nontrialed configuration is likewise free. Since legal response types impose outcome restrictions but no cross-coordinate action restriction, these free actions may be fixed to the displayed values without changing \(B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\), \(h^{32}(t)\), or \(K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\). Every legal full response type has the same observable--target pair as at least one displayed row, because its restricted outcome path has a displayed representative and the four displayed patterns exhaust the two endpoint action bits. Hence the thirty-two displayed combinations form a complete quotient-generating cover; no injectivity or minimality is asserted. The twelve displayed cells are every feasible observable row and each occurs in the table. Consequently the table generates the full observable polytope and cannot omit a column that changes any of the four optima. For every \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\), the programs formed with \(B^{32}\), \(h^{32}\), and \(K^{32}\) satisfy \(L=\pi_1+\pi_2\), \(U=\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4\), \(L_{\mathrm{blind}}=\pi_1\), and \(U_{\mathrm{blind}}=1\). Thus \(p^{32}\) gives \([1/2,3/4]\) versus \([1/4,1]\), while \(p^{32,\circ}\) gives \([397/800,601/800]\) versus \([99/400,1]\). Both laws lie in \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\), since their displayed mixtures give strictly positive weight to every generator of \(\mathfrak O^{32}=B^{32}\Delta_{31}\).
statements.justification: The complete quotient-generating cover, positive generating mixture, and exact arithmetic establish a legally realized and non-boundary two-sided gain without claiming that the displayed cover is injective or minimal.
statements.gap: ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026 reports narrower simulated bounds but gives no sharp action-dependent selective-label quotient-generating cover, exact rational full-versus-blind certificate, or full-polytope relative-interior realization.
statements.consumer: The table is an exact regression fixture for the Imai PSA and aihuman implementations, including every reveal-action pattern and both performance-order directions.
statements.proof_tex:
Use throughout the row and column orders fixed by \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\).  We first verify legality and completeness of the observable--target cover.  For a displayed row with \(z=0\), its neutral-outcome triple is \(111\), while its \(r=1\) triple is one of
\[
000,\qquad 100,\qquad 110,\qquad 111.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus the neutral outcome is constant, the incorrect \(r=1\) outcome is nonincreasing in \(q\), and the correct neutral outcome is at least every incorrect outcome.  These are respectively neutral invariance, incorrect-performance order, and counterfactual correctness in \(\text{def:legal-response-types}\); correct-performance order holds because the correct neutral path is constant.  For a displayed row with \(z=1\), the neutral triple is \(000\), while its correct \(r=1\) triple is one of
\[
000,\qquad 001,\qquad 011,\qquad 111.
\tag{2}
\]
Now the neutral outcome is constant, the correct \(r=1\) outcome is nondecreasing, and every correct outcome is at least the incorrect neutral outcome.  Hence all four restrictions again hold.  Actions are unrestricted by \(\text{def:legal-response-types}\).  The displayed labels and full arrays differ for distinct row indices, so the thirty-two rows are distinct members of \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).

Let \(t\) be any legal type in the specialized design.  Since \(\mathcal S^{32}=\{s_0\}\), its stratum is \(s_0\).  By \(\text{def:32-design-specialization}\) and the incidence definition, \(B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\) reads only
\[
\bigl(A_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_\ell)}\bigr),
\qquad
\bigl(A_{(1,q_h)},Y_{(1,q_h)}\bigr),
\tag{3}
\]
together with \(z\) whenever an endpoint action equals one.  The target \(h^{32}(t)\) reads only \(Y_{(1,q_m)}\).  In particular, neither object reads \(A_{(1,q_m)}\).  Indeed, \(e_{32}\notin J^{32}_0\), so no trial row uses that action, and the target is outcome-only.  The same argument applies to every action coordinate at any other nontrialed configuration.  Since legality restricts outcomes but imposes no cross-coordinate action restriction, these unread action coordinates may be fixed to the table values without changing \(B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\), \(h^{32}(t)\), or \(K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,t}\).

It remains to cover the outcomes read in (3) and at \(q_m\).  If \(z=0\), neutral invariance makes the correct neutral triple constant.  If that constant is zero, correctness forces the incorrect \(r=1\) triple to be \(000\); if it is one, incorrect-performance order permits exactly the four paths in (1).  The neutral-zero case has the same read coordinates as the displayed representative with \(r=1\) path \(000\).  If \(z=1\), the incorrect neutral triple is constant.  If that constant is one, correctness forces the correct \(r=1\) triple to be \(111\); if it is zero, correct-performance order permits exactly the four paths in (2).  The neutral-one case has the same read coordinates as the displayed representative with \(r=1\) path \(111\).  Finally, the four displayed endpoint-action patterns exhaust
\[
\bigl(A_{(1,q_\ell)},A_{(1,q_h)}\bigr)\in\{0,1\}^2.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus every legal full response type has the same \((B^{32}_{\cdot,t},h^{32}(t))\), and consequently the same \((K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,t},h^{32}(t))\), as at least one displayed row.  This proves a complete quotient-generating cover; it does not assert injectivity or minimality of the quotient map.  For example, rows \(1\) and \(17\) have the same observable column and target.  Inspection also shows that every one of the six feasible observable cells in each trial arm occurs.  Hence the twelve displayed cells are exactly the feasible rows, and the table generates the full observable polytope without omitting any column capable of changing one of the four endpoint optima.

We next solve all four programs.  Under \(\pi_3=\pi_2\), direct multiplication of the weights in \(\text{def:32-coordinate-mixture}\) by the two half-incidence entries in each table column gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
p(\pi)=\bigl(&\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,\pi_4/24,\pi_2/2+\pi_4/24,\pi_4/8,
\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2-\pi_4/24,\\
&\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,\pi_4/8,\pi_2/2-\pi_4/24,\pi_4/24,
\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2+\pi_4/24\bigr)^{\top}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
Coarsening revealed labels gives
\[
K^{32}p(\pi)=\bigl(\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12,
\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12,\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,
\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12,\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12\bigr)^{\top}.
\tag{6}
\]
In the full and blind row orders, respectively, define
\[
\lambda_L=(0,0,0,0,0,2,0,0,0,0,2,0)^{\top},
\]
\[
\lambda_U=(0,0,-2,0,0,0,2,2,2,0,2,2)^{\top},
\]
\[
\mu_L=(0,2,0,2,-2,0,-2,0)^{\top},
\qquad
\mu_U=(2,2,2,2,0,0,0,0)^{\top}.
\tag{7}
\]
For every displayed column \(i\), the monotone paths (1)--(2) give
\[
\lambda_L^{\top}B^{32}_{\cdot,i}\leq h^{32}_i
\leq\lambda_U^{\top}B^{32}_{\cdot,i}.
\tag{8}
\]
For the lower inequality, the left side is the indicator of the low-arm cell \((1,1,1)\) plus the indicator of the high-arm cell \((1,1,0)\).  Only the summand whose revealed label matches the unit's label can be nonzero, and the relevant endpoint monotonicity then forces the middle outcome to one.  For the upper inequality, when \(z=0\) the right side is
\(1-\mathbf 1\{A_{(1,q_\ell)}=1,Y_{(1,q_\ell)}=0\}\), and when \(z=1\) it is
\(1-\mathbf 1\{A_{(1,q_h)}=1,Y_{(1,q_h)}=0\}\).  In either case, a middle outcome equal to one forces the relevant endpoint outcome to one by the corresponding performance order.  Likewise, column by column,
\[
\mu_L^{\top}K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,i}
=Y_{(1,q_\ell)}(t_i^{32})+Y_{(1,q_h)}(t_i^{32})-1
\leq h_i^{32}
\leq1
=\mu_U^{\top}K^{32}B^{32}_{\cdot,i}.
\tag{9}
\]
The left inequality in (9) holds for every binary monotone three-point path: if both endpoint values are one, its middle value is one, and otherwise the left side is nonpositive.  The quotient-generating cover shows that (8)--(9) also hold for every omitted legal full type.  With simplex multiplier zero, these are therefore feasible dual certificates.  Multiplying by any feasible type weights and summing, then substituting (5)--(6), gives
\[
L\geq\pi_1+\pi_2,
\qquad
U\leq\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4,
\qquad
L_{\mathrm{blind}}\geq\pi_1,
\qquad
U_{\mathrm{blind}}\leq1.
\tag{10}
\]

We give matching primal certificates.  The notation \(\{i:x,\ldots\}\) below lists the nonzero coordinates of a nonnegative vector.  Put \(r_1=(1,0,0)\), \(r_2=(0,1,0)\), and \(r_3=(0,1,8)\) in \((\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_4)\)-coordinates, and let \(P(r_k)\) be the right side of (5) evaluated at \(r_k\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|l}
X&v_1^X&v_2^X&v_3^X\\\hline
FL&\{32:1\}&\{20:1,32:1\}&
\{3:2/3,6:2,7:2,14:2/3,18:1/3,21:2/3,22:5/3,23:5/3,31:1/3\}\\
FU&\{32:1\}&\{20:1,32:1\}&
\{3:2/3,10:2,11:2,14:2/3,18:1/3,25:2/3,26:5/3,27:5/3,31:1/3\}\\
BL&\{32:1\}&\{8:1,24:1\}&
\{5:8/3,8:7/3,21:8/3,24:7/3\}\\
BU&\{32:1\}&\{12:1,28:1\}&
\{9:8/3,12:7/3,25:8/3,28:7/3\}.
\end{array}
\tag{11}
\]
Adding the two half-incidence entries of each listed column verifies, for \(k=1,2,3\),
\[
B^{32}v_k^{FL}=B^{32}v_k^{FU}=P(r_k),
\qquad
K^{32}B^{32}v_k^{BL}=K^{32}B^{32}v_k^{BU}=K^{32}P(r_k).
\tag{12}
\]
The masses of the vectors for \(k=1,2,3\) are \(1,2,10\), and their target sums are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
X&(h^{32})^{\top}v_1^X&(h^{32})^{\top}v_2^X&(h^{32})^{\top}v_3^X\\\hline
FL&1&1&1\\
FU&1&1&9\\
BL&1&0&0\\
BU&1&2&10.
\end{array}
\tag{13}
\]
For \(X\in\{FL,FU,BL,BU\}\), set
\[
v^X(\pi)=\pi_1v_1^X+\left(\pi_2-\frac{\pi_4}{8}\right)v_2^X
+\frac{\pi_4}{8}v_3^X.
\tag{14}
\]
The coefficients are nonnegative because \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\).  Using \(\pi_3=\pi_2\) and \(\sum_{k=1}^4\pi_k=1\), the mass in (14) is
\[
\pi_1+2\left(\pi_2-\frac{\pi_4}{8}\right)+10\frac{\pi_4}{8}
=\pi_1+2\pi_2+\pi_4=1.
\tag{15}
\]
Moreover,
\[
(\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_4)
=\pi_1r_1+\left(\pi_2-\frac{\pi_4}{8}\right)r_2+\frac{\pi_4}{8}r_3.
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (12), (15), and (16) prove primal feasibility, while (13) gives objectives \(\pi_1+\pi_2\), \(\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4\), \(\pi_1\), and \(1\), respectively.  These reverse all four inequalities in (10).  Therefore
\[
L=\pi_1+\pi_2,
\qquad
U=\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4,
\qquad
L_{\mathrm{blind}}=\pi_1,
\qquad
U_{\mathrm{blind}}=1.
\tag{17}
\]
At \(\pi^{32}=(1,1,1,1)^{\top}/4\), (17) gives \([1/2,3/4]\) versus \([1/4,1]\), and (5) gives the stated vector \(p^{32}\).  At \(\pi^{32,\circ}=(198,199,199,204)^{\top}/800\), it gives \([397/800,601/800]\) versus \([99/400,1]\), and (5) gives the stated vector \(p^{32,\circ}\).

Finally, for every \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\),
\[
\varepsilon_{32}=\frac{\pi_4}{24}>0,
\qquad
a_{32}=\pi_2-\frac{\pi_4}{8}>0,
\qquad
b_{32}=\pi_1+a_{32}>0.
\tag{18}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
30\varepsilon_{32}+a_{32}+b_{32}=\pi_1+2\pi_2+\pi_4=1,
\]
so \(w^{32}(\pi)\) is a probability vector assigning positive mass to every displayed generator.  Aggregate weights of duplicate columns and enumerate the distinct columns as \(b_1,\ldots,b_N\), with aggregate weights \(\beta_k>0\).  Let
\[
V=\operatorname{span}\{b_k-b_1:2\leq k\leq N\},
\qquad
T(x)=\sum_{k=1}^Nx_kb_k
\]
on \(\{x\in\mathbb R^N:\mathbf 1^{\top}x=0\}\).  This linear map is surjective onto \(V\), so it has a linear right inverse \(R\).  If \(V\neq\{0\}\), put \(C=\sup_{\|d\|_2=1}\|Rd\|_\infty<\infty\).  Whenever \(\|d\|_2<\min_k\beta_k/C\), the vector \(\beta+Rd\) is nonnegative, has mass one, and maps to \(\sum_k\beta_kb_k+d\).  If \(V=\{0\}\), the relative domain is a singleton.  In either case, the induced law has a neighborhood in the affine hull contained in \(\mathfrak O^{32}\), so it belongs to \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\).  This applies to both displayed choices of \(\pi\).  By \(\text{thm:finite-response-converse}\), each matching primal certificate in (14) canonically produces a legal SCM attaining its objective.  Hence (17) gives sharp causal endpoints rather than extrema of an unrelated algebraic program.

statements.statement: There is a nonempty relatively open set \(\mathcal U\subset\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\) containing \(p^{32,\circ}\) such that \(L(p)>L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p)\) and \(U(p)<U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p)\) for every \(p\in\mathcal U\). The conclusion follows from the two strict gaps \(199/800\) at \(p^{32,\circ}\) and continuity of the four finite-polyhedral value functions on relative interior.
statements.justification: This is the balanced thirty-two-type corollary of the general dual-face characterization and primitive bracket-stratum theorem.
statements.gap: The general theorem, rather than this corollary alone, supplies the arbitrary-finite-design characterization absent from the comparison literature.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts retain the exact rational regression fixture and a stable local neighborhood for implementation checks.
statements.proof_tex:
The balanced singleton-stratum design in \(\text{def:32-design-specialization}\) satisfies \(\mathsf{Bracket}_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\): take \(s_*=s_0\), use \(q_\ell<q_m<q_h\), and observe that the two trial arms have probabilities \(1/2>0\).  By \(\text{thm:complete-32-type-refinement-certificate}\), at \(p_0=p^{32,\circ}\),
\[
L(p_0)-L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p_0)
=\frac{397-198}{800}=\frac{199}{800}>0,
\]
\[
U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p_0)-U(p_0)
=\frac{800-601}{800}=\frac{199}{800}>0.
\tag{1}
\]
The same certificate proves \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\).  By \(\text{thm:general-dual-face-strict-refinement-characterization}\), the two strict inequalities define a relatively open subset of \(\mathfrak O^{32}\).  The relative interior is itself relatively open in \(\mathfrak O^{32}\).  Therefore the intersection of these two open sets is a relatively open set \(\mathcal U\subset\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\).  It contains \(p_0\) by (1), so it is nonempty, and every \(p\in\mathcal U\) satisfies both asserted strict refinements.

statements.statement: Applying the generic simultaneous-region propagation of DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024, Section 6 and Appendix E, to the SLCC incidence program gives \(\Pr_p\{[L(p),U(p)]\subseteq\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\ge1\) and \(p\in\mathfrak O\). On \(p\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\), the intersection \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathfrak O\) is nonempty and the implementation optima are attained.
statements.justification: This implementation corollary supplies an exact conservative reporting procedure while acknowledging the generic propagation theorem as prior art.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024, Section 6 and Appendix E, already establish generic confidence-region propagation; the contribution here is its explicit implementation for the SLCC incidence map, not a new inference principle.
statements.consumer: The aihuman analysis can report a finite-sample envelope for the entire sharp PSA deployment interval.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\) and \(n\geq1\).  For each cell \(o\in\mathcal O\), the indicator variables \(\mathbf 1\{O_i=o\}\) are independent Bernoulli variables with success probability \(p_o\) under \(\text{ass:iid-finite-sampling}\).  Hence
\[
N_o=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{O_i=o\}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p_o).
\tag{1}
\]
By the defining inversion of the two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval at error \(\alpha/|\mathcal O|\), each marginal interval obeys
\[
\Pr_p\{p_o\notin[\ell_o(N_o),u_o(N_o)]\}
\leq\frac{\alpha}{|\mathcal O|}.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, its lower endpoint is obtained by inverting the upper-tail binomial test and its upper endpoint by inverting the lower-tail test, each at half the displayed marginal error; the two rejection probabilities sum to at most \(\alpha/|\mathcal O|\).  No independence among the counts is used.  The union bound applied to (2) gives
\[
\Pr_p\{p\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}
\geq1-\sum_{o\in\mathcal O}\frac{\alpha}{|\mathcal O|}
=1-\alpha.
\tag{3}
\]

On the event \(p\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\), we also have \(p\in\mathfrak O\), so \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathfrak O\neq\varnothing\).  Every \(v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) satisfying \(Bv=p\) is then feasible for the confidence optimization.  By \(\text{prop:sharp-selective-label-interval}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
[L(p),U(p)]
&=\{h_e^{\top}v:v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}},\ Bv=p\}\\
&\subseteq
\{h_e^{\top}v:v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}},\ Bv\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}
=\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
If the intersection is empty, \(\text{def:whole-set-confidence-construction}\) returns \([0,1]\), which contains the identified set because \(h_e\) is binary and the latent weights form a probability vector.  Combining (3)--(4) yields
\[
\Pr_p\{[L(p),U(p)]\subseteq\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
Finally, whenever \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathfrak O\neq\varnothing\), the feasible weight set is nonempty because \(\mathfrak O=B\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  It is a closed subset of the compact simplex, since \(B\) is linear and \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) is closed.  Its linear image under \(v\mapsto h_e^{\top}v\) is therefore a compact interval, so both implementation optima are attained.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the map \(x\mapsto\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}x)\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(p\) with derivative \(\Gamma'_p\), and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta-\theta(p)\}\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p)\). This formula remains valid when \(p\) is on a projection face and either endpoint has multiple optimal bases.
statements.justification: The limit law exposes both sources of nonregularity instead of imposing margin conditions that remove simultaneous ties.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019, Theorem 2.1 and Section 4, supplies the directional delta method and projection derivative; ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026, Theorem 5.1, assumes margin separation. The new formula composes the observable-polytope projection with both LP optimal-face maps for this causal identified set.
statements.consumer: It supplies pointwise standard-error simulation and diagnoses exactly when ordinary Gaussian endpoint intervals fail in finite human--AI trials.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(d=|\mathcal O|\) and \(\Phi=\theta\circ\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\).  We first differentiate the Euclidean projection without an interior-point assumption.  Let \(t_k\downarrow0\), let \(g_k\to g\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), and set
\[
x_k=p+t_kg_k,
\qquad
q_k=\Pi_{\mathfrak O}(x_k),
\qquad
d_k=\frac{q_k-p}{t_k}.
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the minimizing property of \(q_k\) gives
\[
\|q_k-x_k\|_2\leq\|p-x_k\|_2=t_k\|g_k\|_2,
\]
and hence \(\|d_k\|_2\leq2\|g_k\|_2\).  Thus \((d_k)\) is bounded.  Projection onto the nonempty closed convex polytope \(\mathfrak O\) is characterized by the first-order inequality
\[
\langle x_k-q_k,v-q_k\rangle\leq0
\qquad(v\in\mathfrak O).
\tag{2}
\]
Every subsequential limit \(d_*\) of \((d_k)\) belongs to \(T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\) by the definition of that closed tangent cone.  If \(z\) is radial, meaning \(p+\varepsilon z\in\mathfrak O\) for some \(\varepsilon>0\), convexity implies \(p+t_kz\in\mathfrak O\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).  Substitute this point for \(v\) in (2), divide by \(t_k^2\), and pass along a subsequence for which \(d_k\to d_*\).  This gives
\[
\langle g-d_*,z-d_*\rangle\leq0.
\tag{3}
\]
Radial directions are dense in \(T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\) by its defining closure, so (3) holds for every \(z\) in that cone.  Expanding squared distances shows that (3) is equivalent to
\[
\|g-d_*\|_2\leq\|g-z\|_2
\qquad(z\in T_{\mathfrak O}(p)).
\]
Strict convexity gives the unique minimizer, so
\[
d_*=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g.
\tag{4}
\]
Every convergent subsequence has the same limit and the original sequence is bounded; hence the whole sequence converges to (4).  This proves Hadamard directional differentiability of \(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\) at \(p\), with derivative \(g\mapsto\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).

We next derive the endpoint derivatives from finiteness.  The observable--target set
\[
\mathcal C=\operatorname{conv}\{(B_{\cdot,t},h_e(t)):t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}
\tag{5}
\]
is a finite polytope.  Eliminating the finitely many simplex coordinates from its defining finite system of linear equalities and inequalities gives a finite half-space representation of \(\mathcal C\).  Solving those inequalities for the last coordinate shows that there are finite index sets \(R_L,R_U\) and dual-feasible affine functions
\[
\ell_r(x)=\alpha_r+\lambda_r^{\top}x\quad(r\in R_L),
\qquad
u_s(x)=\bar\alpha_s+\bar\lambda_s^{\top}x\quad(s\in R_U)
\]
such that, throughout \(\mathfrak O\),
\[
L(x)=\max_{r\in R_L}\ell_r(x),
\qquad
U(x)=\min_{s\in R_U}u_s(x).
\tag{6}
\]
For completeness, dual feasibility follows by evaluating each supporting inequality on every generator in (5): it gives \(\alpha_r\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\lambda_r\leq h_e\) for lower supports and \(\bar\alpha_s\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\bar\lambda_s\geq h_e\) for upper supports.  Conversely, multiplying either columnwise inequality by feasible simplex weights proves weak duality, so the active supports in (6) attain the corresponding dual value.

Let
\[
R_L(p)=\{r:\ell_r(p)=L(p)\},
\qquad
R_U(p)=\{s:u_s(p)=U(p)\}.
\]
Because the families are finite, every inactive affine function has a strictly positive gap at \(p\).  Hence, if \(z_k\to z\) and \(p+t_kz_k\in\mathfrak O\), inactive indices cannot optimize for all sufficiently large \(k\), and
\[
\frac{L(p+t_kz_k)-L(p)}{t_k}
\longrightarrow\max_{r\in R_L(p)}\lambda_r^{\top}z,
\tag{7}
\]
\[
\frac{U(p+t_kz_k)-U(p)}{t_k}
\longrightarrow\min_{s\in R_U(p)}\bar\lambda_s^{\top}z.
\tag{8}
\]
These finite active-index formulas agree with optimization over the entire unnormalized optimal faces.  Indeed, if \((\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)\), dual feasibility gives
\[
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}(p+t_kz_k)\leq L(p+t_kz_k),
\qquad
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p=L(p).
\]
Subtract, divide by \(t_k\), and use (7) to obtain
\[
\lambda^{\top}z\leq\max_{r\in R_L(p)}\lambda_r^{\top}z.
\]
Every active pair in (7) belongs to \(\Lambda_L(p)\), so equality holds after maximizing over the full face.  The analogous upper-dual argument gives
\[
L'_p(z)=\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z,
\qquad
U'_p(z)=\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z.
\tag{9}
\]
These expressions are gauge invariant on the tangent cone: every \(z\in T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\) satisfies \(\mathbf 1^{\top}z=0\), and replacing \((\alpha,\lambda)\) by \((\alpha-c,\lambda+c\mathbf 1)\) leaves \(\lambda^{\top}z\) unchanged.

For the sequence in (1), equation (4) gives \(d_k\to z=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).  Apply (7)--(9) to \(q_k=p+t_kd_k\).  We obtain
\[
\frac{\Phi(p+t_kg_k)-\Phi(p)}{t_k}
\longrightarrow
\left(
\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z,
\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z
\right)
=\Gamma'_p(g).
\tag{10}
\]
Thus \(\Phi\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(p\).  The derivative is continuous because projection onto a closed convex cone is nonexpansive and the two endpoint coordinates in (9) are finite piecewise-linear functions on the tangent cone.  Multiple active projection faces and multiple optimal LP bases remain inside the projection, maximum, and minimum in (10).

It remains to derive the stochastic limit.  Under \(\text{ass:iid-finite-sampling}\), write \(X_i=\mathbf e_{O_i}-p\).  These vectors are independent, centered, bounded, and have covariance \(\Sigma_p\).  For every \(a\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(u\in\mathbb R\), Taylor expansion with a remainder bounded uniformly by a constant times \(n^{-3/2}|a^{\top}X_i|^3\) gives
\[
\mathbb E\exp\!\left(\frac{iu a^{\top}X_i}{\sqrt n}\right)
=1-\frac{u^2a^{\top}\Sigma_pa}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Raising this characteristic function to the \(n\)-th power yields
\[
\mathbb E\exp\!\left(iu a^{\top}\sqrt n(\widehat p-p)\right)
\longrightarrow\exp\!\left(-\frac{u^2a^{\top}\Sigma_pa}{2}\right).
\tag{11}
\]
Thus every linear contrast converges to the corresponding contrast of \(G_p\), including zero-variance contrasts, and the joint characteristic functions converge to that of \(G_p\).  Hence
\[
X_n:=\sqrt n(\widehat p-p)\rightsquigarrow G_p.
\tag{12}
\]

Define \(f_n(g)=\sqrt n\{\Phi(p+g/\sqrt n)-\Phi(p)\}\).  Equation (10) says that whenever \(g_n\to g\), one has \(f_n(g_n)\to\Gamma'_p(g)\).  This sequential property is uniform on every compact set: otherwise a violating sequence in a compact set would have a convergent subsequence contradicting (10) and continuity of \(\Gamma'_p\).  Since (12) makes \((X_n)\) tight, for every bounded continuous test function \(\psi\), uniform convergence on a compact set carrying arbitrarily high probability gives
\[
\mathbb E\psi(f_n(X_n))-\mathbb E\psi(\Gamma'_p(X_n))\longrightarrow0.
\]
Continuity of \(\Gamma'_p\) and (12) give \(\Gamma'_p(X_n)\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p)\).  Since \(p\in\mathfrak O\), \(\Phi(p)=\theta(p)\), and \(\text{def:projection-endpoint-estimator}\) gives \(\Phi(\widehat p)=\widehat\theta\).  Therefore
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta-\theta(p)\}
\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p),
\]
with no projection-face or optimal-basis uniqueness assumption.

statements.statement: If there is \(j^{\star}\in J_0\) with \(c_e(s)=c_{j^{\star}}(s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), then \(L(p)=U(p)=\mathbb E[Y\mid D=j^{\star}]\). Separately, if \(A_c=1\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\), then \(Z\) is fully observed, but full revelation alone does not point-identify every distinct untrialed configuration: there exist two legal SCMs with the same fully labeled trial law and different untrialed means. Identification may nevertheless occur at special observed laws, through configuration overlap, through the neutral-invariance restriction, or under further identifying restrictions.
statements.justification: The sanity check recovers ordinary randomized identification exactly under configuration equality and keeps full revelation logically separate from policy overlap.
statements.gap: ImaiJiangGreinerHalenShin2023 identifies observed randomized recommendation arms; the reduction embeds precisely that case and makes no universal identification claim for a distinct untrialed configuration.
statements.consumer: Implementations can test the standard RCT case without falsely declaring identification merely because all labels are revealed.
statements.proof_tex:
Suppose first that \(c_e(s)=c_{j^\star}(s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), where \(j^\star\in J_0\).  Then for every legal response type,
\[
h_e(t)=y_{c_e(s_t)}(t)=y_{c_{j^\star}(s_t)}(t).
\tag{1}
\]
The known arm law has \(\rho_{j^\star}>0\) because \(\rho\) lies in the relative interior of the trial-arm simplex.  For every compatible latent mixture \(v\), randomized assignment and the common-outcome response imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_v[Y\mid D=j^\star]
&=\rho_{j^\star}^{-1}
\sum_t v_t\rho_{j^\star}y_{c_{j^\star}(s_t)}(t)\\
&=h_e^{\top}v,
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
where (1) was used in the last equality.  The conditional mean on the left of (2) is determined by the observed law \(p\).  Consequently every \(v\) in the fiber \(\{v:Bv=p\}\) has the same target, and \(\text{prop:sharp-selective-label-interval}\) gives
\[
L(p)=U(p)=\mathbb E[Y\mid D=j^\star].
\]

For the separate revelation claim, if \(A_c=1\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\), then the reveal-action assumption gives \(R=1\), and masked truth gives \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=Z\) almost surely.  Full revelation does not by itself identify a distinct untrialed configuration.  Consider one stratum, one trialed configuration \((1,q_\ell)\), one untrialed configuration \((1,q_h)\), and \(q_\ell<q_h\).  In two deterministic SCMs set \(Z=1\), set every action response to one, and set every neutral outcome to zero.  For the \(r=1\) outcome path, set
\[
(Y_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_h)})=(0,0)
\quad\text{in the first model},
\qquad
(Y_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_h)})=(0,1)
\quad\text{in the second}.
\tag{3}
\]
Both paths are nondecreasing, as correct-performance order requires for \(Z=1\).  The incorrect neutral path is constant, so neutral invariance and incorrect-performance order hold, and the correct outcomes dominate the neutral outcomes, so counterfactual correctness holds.  Both models can use the same randomized arm law and therefore belong to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  Their trialed laws, including the always-revealed label \(Z=1\), coincide because both have trialed outcome zero; their untrialed means are respectively zero and one by (3).  This proves nonidentification from full revelation alone, while the first part proves identification under configuration overlap.  Special observed fibers, neutral-invariance coincidences, or additional restrictions may still collapse the sharp interval, exactly as the statement allows.

statements.statement:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\), put \(\beta=1-\alpha\), write \((D_L,D_U)=\Gamma'_p\), and define \(H(g)=\max\{D_L(g),-D_U(g)\}\).  Let
\[
V_p=\{g:\mathbf 1^{\top}g=0,\ g_o=0\text{ whenever }p_o=0\}.
\]
Suppose the active projection cones and extreme slopes of \(\Lambda_L(p)\) and \(\Lambda_U(p)\), refined by their zero and comparison hyperplanes, yield a finite polyhedral fan on \(V_p\) such that: (i) locally,
\[
\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}(p+x))-\theta(p)=(D_L(x),D_U(x)),
\]
with both coordinates linear on each fan cone; and (ii) every retained facet normal and endpoint slope is nonzero on \(V_p\).  Let \(\mathcal A_p\) be the finite closure under row selection and sign changes of matrices whose rows are the restrictions to \(V_p\) of those retained normals and slopes.  With \(\mathbf e_o\) denoting the standard basis vector of observable cell \(o\), define, from an independent size-\(m\) categorical sample,
\[
X_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m(\mathbf e_{O_i}-p),
\qquad
\delta_m(p)=\max_{A\in\mathcal A_p}\sup_x
\left|\Pr_p\{AX_m\leq x\}-\Pr\{AG_p\leq x\}\right|.
\]
Assume Gaussian nondegeneracy on \(V_p\):
\[
v^{\top}\Sigma_pv>0\quad\text{for every nonzero }v\in V_p.
\]
Use the fixed schedules
\[
m_n=\max\{1,\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\},
\qquad
\eta_n=\min\{\alpha/2,n^{-1/12}\},
\]
and let \(c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}\) be the lower conditional \((1-\alpha+\eta_n)\)-quantile specified in \(\text{def:atomic-tie-subsampling-handle}\).  Then \(C(p)<\infty\), \(\delta_m(p)\leq C(p)m^{-1/2}\), every atom of \(H(G_p)\) is at zero, and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr_p\left\{
L(p)\geq\widehat L-\frac{c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}}{\sqrt n},
\quad
U(p)\leq\widehat U+\frac{c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}}{\sqrt n}
\right\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
No projection-cone or LP-basis uniqueness, and no restriction on full-dimensional fan cones where \(H\) vanishes, is required.  The constant and the finite Boolean-event family are fixed-law objects and need not be uniform as \(p\) approaches covariance-rank changes.

The atomic case is nonvacuous in the thirty-two-type table.  At
\[
p_\dagger=\tfrac12(B^{32}_{\cdot,3}+B^{32}_{\cdot,5})
=\tfrac14(\mathbf e_2+\mathbf e_3+2\mathbf e_7),
\]
both endpoint programs have distinct optimal slopes and the observable law lies on a nontrivial projection face.  The exact certificate in \(\text{prop:32-nondegenerate-atomic-tie-certificate}\) gives relatively open regions on which \(H=0\) and \(H>0\), respectively, and hence
\[
0<\Pr\{H(G_{p_\dagger})=0\}<1.
\]

statements.proof_tex:
Let \(d=|\mathcal O|\), put \(\Phi=\theta\circ\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\), and define
\[
X_n=\sqrt n(\widehat p-p),
\qquad
T_n=\max\{\sqrt n(\widehat L-L(p)),\sqrt n(U(p)-\widehat U)\}.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\text{lem:finite-multinomial-clt}\), under \(\text{ass:iid-finite-sampling}\),
\[
X_n\rightsquigarrow G_p,
\qquad
X_n=O_{\Pr}(1).
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover, \(X_n\in V_p\) almost surely: its coordinates sum to zero, and if \(p_o=0\), then the nonnegative count \(N_o\) equals zero almost surely.

By the local finite-fan hypothesis, there is \(r>0\) such that
\[
\Phi(p+x)-\Phi(p)=(D_L(x),D_U(x))
\quad\text{for }x\in V_p\text{ with }\|x\|_2<r.
\tag{3}
\]
Both coordinates are continuous, positively homogeneous, and linear on finitely many fan cones.  Hence there is \(C_D<\infty\) such that
\[
|D_L(x)|\vee|D_U(x)|\leq C_D\|x\|_2
\qquad(x\in V_p).
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4), consistently with \(\text{thm:projection-composed-directional-limit}\), imply
\[
T_n=H(X_n)
\tag{5}
\]
with probability tending to one, and \(H(X_n)\rightsquigarrow H(G_p)\).

Put \(m=m_n\).  Conditional on the full sample, let \(\widehat p_b\) be the empirical law of a uniformly selected size-\(m\) subsample without replacement, and define
\[
a_n=\sqrt m(\widehat p-p)=\sqrt{m/n}\,X_n.
\tag{6}
\]
When both empirical laws lie in the neighborhood in (3), the centered subsampling statistic whose conditional lower quantile defines \(c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}\) equals
\[
S_{n,b}=\max\left\{
D_L\bigl(\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p)\bigr)-D_L(a_n),
D_U(a_n)-D_U\bigl(\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p)\bigr)
\right\}.
\tag{7}
\]
This follows by applying (3) separately at \(\widehat p_b\) and \(\widehat p\), subtracting the two endpoint coordinates, multiplying by \(\sqrt m\), and using positive homogeneity.

We compare (7) to an independent size-\(m\) experiment.  Couple the ordered indices sampled without replacement to \(m\) indices sampled with replacement from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).  Coupling fails only if two with-replacement indices coincide, so the union bound gives conditional failure probability at most
\[
\frac{m(m-1)}{2n}.
\tag{8}
\]
Conditional on the data, a with-replacement observation has law \(\widehat p\).  Couple each such observation maximally to an independent draw from \(p\).  The one-draw mismatch probability is
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\widehat p,p)=\frac12\|\widehat p-p\|_1,
\]
so another union bound gives total mismatch probability at most
\[
\frac m2\|\widehat p-p\|_1.
\tag{9}
\]
On \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M\}\), (9) is at most \(m\sqrt d M/(2\sqrt n)\).

On the successful coupling event, \(\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p)\) equals
\[
X_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m(\mathbf e_{O_i}-p)
\]
for an independent size-\(m\) sample, and (7) becomes
\[
K_{a_n}(X_m),
\qquad
K_a(g)=\max\{D_L(g)-D_L(a),D_U(a)-D_U(g)\}.
\tag{10}
\]
The localization failure is exponentially small.  Each coordinate of \(\mathbf e_{O_i}-p\) is centered and bounded by one in absolute value.  Applying the exponential Markov inequality to each coordinate and taking a finite union gives constants \(C_0,c_0>0\), depending only on the fixed law and the neighborhood, such that
\[
\Pr_p\{\|X_m\|_2>r\sqrt m/2\}\leq C_0e^{-c_0m}.
\tag{11}
\]
For fixed \(M\), equations (6), (8)--(11) bound the conditional coupling and localization error on \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M\}\) by
\[
q_{n,M}=\frac{m(m-1)}{2n}
+\frac{m\sqrt d M}{2\sqrt n}+C_0e^{-c_0m}.
\tag{12}
\]

On each pair of refined fan cones containing \(a\) and \(g\), the event \(K_a(g)\leq x\) is an intersection of finitely many linear inequalities.  The finite union over cone pairs is a finite Boolean combination of lower orthants whose row matrices belong to \(\mathcal A_p\).  Finite inclusion--exclusion and \(\text{lem:finite-alphabet-fan-berry-esseen-explicit-schedule}\) therefore bound the independent-multinomial to Gaussian comparison by a fixed finite multiple of
\[
\delta_m(p)\leq C(p)m^{-1/2}.
\tag{13}
\]
Rank-zero row families contribute no error because their linear images are deterministically zero.  This is the effective-range step needed when \(\Sigma_p\) is singular.

Equation (4) also gives, for every \(a,g\in V_p\),
\[
|K_a(g)-H(g)|
\leq |D_L(a)|\vee|D_U(a)|
\leq C_D\|a\|_2.
\tag{14}
\]
On \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M\}\), the right side at \(a=a_n\) is at most \(C_DM\sqrt{m/n}\).  Every nonzero normal and endpoint slope retained in \(\mathcal A_p\) has positive Gaussian variance by nondegeneracy on \(V_p\); its Gaussian image therefore has a bounded density.  The Gaussian probability of each slab introduced by the displacement in (14) is bounded by a fixed multiple of \(\sqrt{m/n}\), and hence by a fixed multiple of \(m/\sqrt n\).

For the fixed schedules, \(\text{lem:finite-alphabet-fan-berry-esseen-explicit-schedule}\) gives
\[
\delta_m(p)=O(n^{-1/6}),
\qquad
\frac m{\sqrt n}=O(n^{-1/6}),
\qquad
\frac{m^2}{n}=O(n^{-1/3}),
\qquad
e^{-c_0m}=O(e^{-c'n^{1/3}})
\tag{15}
\]
for some \(c'>0\).  Since \(\eta_n=n^{-1/12}\) eventually, every term in (15) is \(o(\eta_n)\).  Combining (2) and (12)--(15), and then letting \(M\to\infty\), proves at every continuity point \(x\) of the law of \(H(G_p)\) that
\[
\Pr^*\{S_{n,b}\leq x\}\longrightarrow
F(x):=\Pr\{H(G_p)\leq x\}
\quad\text{in probability},
\tag{16}
\]
where \(\Pr^*\) is conditional probability given the full sample.

On the relative interior of each full-dimensional cone of the fan refined by endpoint-comparison and zero hyperplanes, \(H\) is one homogeneous linear functional.  Cone boundaries lie in finitely many proper hyperplanes whose normals are nonzero on \(V_p\); Gaussian nondegeneracy makes their probabilities zero.  A nonzero linear functional of \(G_p\) has a continuous Gaussian law, while a zero linear functional is identically zero.  It follows that
\[
F\text{ can have an atom only at }0.
\tag{17}
\]

Write \(\beta=1-\alpha\), let \(c_n=c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,\beta+\eta_n}\), using the lower-quantile convention, and put \(q_\beta=\inf\{x:F(x)\geq\beta\}\).  Suppose first that \(q_\beta\neq0\).  For every sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), choose the continuity point \(x_\varepsilon=q_\beta-\varepsilon\); by the definition of the lower quantile, \(F(x_\varepsilon)<\beta\).  Equation (16) and \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) imply \(\Pr\{c_n>x_\varepsilon\}\to1\).  Combining this with (5), weak convergence, and continuity of \(F\) at the nonzero point \(q_\beta\), then letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), gives
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr_p\{T_n\leq c_n\}
\geq F(q_\beta)\geq\beta.
\tag{18}
\]

It remains to treat \(q_\beta=0\), where
\[
F(0-)\leq\beta\leq F(0).
\tag{19}
\]
If \(H(X_n)=0\), positive homogeneity and (6) imply
\[
D_L(a_n)\leq0,
\qquad
D_U(a_n)\geq0.
\tag{20}
\]
For every \(g\in V_p\), the global sign implication
\[
\begin{aligned}
K_{a_n}(g)<0
&\Longrightarrow D_L(g)<D_L(a_n)\leq0
\ \text{and}\ D_U(g)>D_U(a_n)\geq0\\
&\Longrightarrow H(g)<0
\end{aligned}
\tag{21}
\]
uses neither a selected projection cone nor a unique endpoint slope.  The event \(\{H(g)<0\}\) is a finite union of intersections of strict half-spaces from the refined fan.  Approximation from below, finite inclusion--exclusion, and the same coupling comparison as in (12)--(13) therefore give, uniformly on \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M,H(X_n)=0\}\),
\[
\Pr^*\{S_{n,b}<0\}
\leq F(0-)+O(\delta_m(p))+O_M(m/\sqrt n)
+O(m^2/n)+O(e^{-c_0m}).
\tag{22}
\]
By (15), the error in (22) is \(o(\eta_n)\).  If \(F(0-)<\beta\), it is eventually smaller than the fixed gap to \(\beta\); if \(F(0-)=\beta\), it is smaller than the quantile slack \(\eta_n\) with probability tending to one.  A lower \((\beta+\eta_n)\)-quantile is nonnegative whenever the conditional mass strictly below zero is less than \(\beta+\eta_n\).  Letting \(M\to\infty\) using (2), we obtain
\[
\Pr_p\{H(X_n)=0,\ c_n<0\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{23}
\]

We also have \(c_n=o_{\Pr}(1)\).  For every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(F(-\varepsilon)<\beta\), so (16) gives \(\Pr\{c_n> -\varepsilon\}\to1\).  Moreover, \(F(\varepsilon)>\beta\).  This is immediate if \(F(0)>\beta\).  If \(F(0)=\beta\) and \(H\) takes a positive value, continuity, positive homogeneity, and Gaussian full support on \(V_p\) give positive probability to \(0<H(G_p)\leq\varepsilon\).  If \(H\) takes no positive value, then \(F(\varepsilon)=1\).  Another use of (16) gives \(\Pr\{c_n\leq\varepsilon\}\to1\).  Therefore
\[
c_n=o_{\Pr}(1).
\tag{24}
\]

The zero set of \(H\) is a finite union of interiors of full-dimensional zero cones and subsets of finitely many proper fan hyperplanes.  Its boundary is Gaussian-null by nondegeneracy, so it is a continuity set for (2).  Consequently
\[
\Pr_p\{H(X_n)=0\}\longrightarrow F(0)-F(0-).
\tag{25}
\]
For each \(\varepsilon>0\), equations (5), (23), and (24) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr_p\{T_n\leq c_n\}
&\geq \lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_p\{H(X_n)\leq-\varepsilon\}\\
&\quad+\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_p\{H(X_n)=0\}\\
&=F(-\varepsilon)+F(0)-F(0-).
\end{aligned}
\]
Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) makes the right side \(F(0)\geq\beta\).  Together with (18),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr_p\{T_n\leq c_n\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{26}
\]
By (1), the event in (26) is exactly
\[
L(p)\geq\widehat L-\frac{c_n}{\sqrt n},
\qquad
U(p)\leq\widehat U+\frac{c_n}{\sqrt n}.
\]
The quantile level is well typed because \(0<\eta_n\leq\alpha/2\), so \(0<1-\alpha+\eta_n<1\).

Finally, \(\text{prop:32-nondegenerate-atomic-tie-certificate}\) supplies the exact early-kill verification at \(p_\dagger\).  Its tangent representations, all-column polar inequalities, matching feasible type-weight directions, and all-column dual certificates establish
\[
(D_L,D_U,H)(g_0)=(0,6/5,0),
\qquad
(D_L,D_U,H)(g_1)=(12/5,0,12/5).
\]
It also proves that both endpoint faces contain distinct slopes, that the projection face is nontrivial, and that there are relatively open zero and positive regions.  Since \(\Sigma_{p_\dagger}\) is positive definite on the two-dimensional space \(V_{p_\dagger}\), both regions have positive Gaussian probability.  Hence
\[
0<\Pr\{H(G_{p_\dagger})=0\}<1,
\]
which proves nonvacuity without projection-cone or LP-basis uniqueness.

statements.statement:
Let \(B\) have finitely many columns \(b_t\), let \(h_e(t)\in\{0,1\}\), and let \(\mathfrak O=B\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  The lower and upper programs attain their optima.  Moreover,
\[
L(p)=\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_L}\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\},
\qquad
U(p)=\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_U}\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\},
\]
and both optimal faces are nonempty for every \(p\in\mathfrak O\).  The four value functions obtained from \(B\) and \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}B\) are finite piecewise-affine functions, continuous on their entire relative domains.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(b_t=B_{\cdot,t}\), \(h_t=h_e(t)\), and form the finite observable--target hull
\[
\mathcal C=\{(Bv,h_e^{\top}v):v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}
=\operatorname{conv}\{(b_t,h_t):t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The simplex is compact and the map in (1) is linear.  Therefore \(\mathcal C\), every fiber \(\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:Bv=p\}\), and its image under \(v\mapsto h_e^{\top}v\) are compact.  For \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the last image is also nonempty and convex, hence a compact interval.  Its endpoints are attained and equal \(L(p)\) and \(U(p)\) by \(\text{def:sharp-endpoint-programs}\).

We derive duality without silently normalizing the mass multiplier.  The membership condition \((x,z)\in\mathcal C\) is the finite linear system
\[
v_t\geq0\quad(t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}),
\qquad
\mathbf 1^{\top}v=1,
\qquad
Bv=x,
\qquad
h_e^{\top}v=z.
\tag{2}
\]
Replace equalities by pairs of inequalities and eliminate the coordinates of \(v\) successively.  At each elimination step, inequalities with positive coefficient give upper bounds, those with negative coefficient give lower bounds, and those with zero coefficient remain; existence of the eliminated coordinate is equivalent to every retained lower bound being at most every retained upper bound.  Thus each step preserves equivalence and finiteness.  After finitely many steps, there exist finite \(R\), vectors \(a_r\), and scalars \(d_r,c_r\) such that
\[
\mathcal C=\{(x,z):a_r^{\top}x+d_rz\leq c_r\text{ for every }r\in R\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The valid inequalities \(-z\leq0\) and \(z\leq1\), which follow from \(h_t\in\{0,1\}\), may be added to (3).  Hence \(R_-:=\{r:d_r<0\}\) and \(R_+:=\{r:d_r>0\}\) are nonempty.  For fixed \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the constraints with \(d_r=0\) are already satisfied, and solving (3) for \(z\) gives
\[
L(p)=\max_{r\in R_-}\frac{c_r-a_r^{\top}p}{d_r},
\qquad
U(p)=\min_{r\in R_+}\frac{c_r-a_r^{\top}p}{d_r}.
\tag{4}
\]

For \(r\in R_-\), write its affine function in (4) as \(\alpha_r+\lambda_r^{\top}p\).  Substituting every generator \((b_t,h_t)\) into the defining inequality in (3), and dividing by \(d_r<0\), gives
\[
\alpha_r+\lambda_r^{\top}b_t\leq h_t
\qquad\text{for every }t.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus \((\alpha_r,\lambda_r)\in\mathcal D_L\).  Conversely, if \((\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_L\) and \(Bv=p\), then
\[
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p
=\sum_t v_t(\alpha+\lambda^{\top}b_t)
\leq\sum_tv_th_t=h_e^{\top}v.
\tag{6}
\]
Taking the minimum in (6) and then choosing an index attaining the finite maximum in (4) proves
\[
L(p)=\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_L}
\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\},
\tag{7}
\]
and exhibits at least one optimizer.  Repeating (5)--(7) for \(r\in R_+\), with inequalities reversed after division by \(d_r>0\), gives
\[
U(p)=\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_U}
\{\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\},
\tag{8}
\]
again with attainment.

Equation (4) is a maximum or minimum of finitely many affine functions.  Therefore \(L\) and \(U\) are finite piecewise-affine and continuous on all of their relative domain \(\mathfrak O\), including its boundary.  Applying exactly the same argument to the finite matrix \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}B\) proves attainment, finite-polyhedral duality, and continuity for \(L_{\mathrm{blind}}\) and \(U_{\mathrm{blind}}\) on \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\mathfrak O\).

statements.statement:
For every finite selective-label incidence model and every \(p\in\mathfrak O\),
\[
L(p)>L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_L(p)\cap\mathcal E_K=\varnothing,
\]
and
\[
U(p)<U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_U(p)\cap\mathcal E_K=\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, the lower inequality is strict exactly when the linear system
\[
\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\lambda\leq h_e,\qquad
\lambda=K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu,\qquad
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p=L(p)
\]
is infeasible, and the upper inequality is strict exactly when the system obtained by replacing \(\leq,L\) with \(\geq,U\) is infeasible.  Consequently \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}\) is relatively open in \(\mathfrak O\).  If \(\mathsf{Bracket}_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) holds, then \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}\cap\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O)\) is nonempty and contains a nonempty relatively open subset of \(\mathfrak O\).  A law supported on the bracket stratum has both full-versus-blind gaps equal to \(199/800\); mixing it by a sufficiently small positive amount with any law assigning positive mass to every legal response type gives the asserted relative-interior region.  Duplicate low- or high-performance arms, arbitrary positive randomization probabilities, additional performance values, other strata, and configurations away from the bracket stratum do not invalidate this construction.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\).  By \(\text{lem:finite-incidence-duality-continuity}\), the full lower dual optimum is attained on \(\Lambda_L(p)\), while the blind lower dual is
\[
\max_{\alpha,\mu}\left\{\alpha+\mu^{\top}K_{\mathrm{blind}}p:
\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu\leq h_e\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Under the substitution \(\lambda=K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu\), the feasible set in (1) is exactly \(\mathcal D_L\cap\mathcal E_K\), and its objective is \(\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p\).  Thus (1) restricts the full lower-dual objective to the embedded blind subset.  Attainment of both finite programs implies
\[
L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)=L(p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_L(p)\cap\mathcal E_K\neq\varnothing.
\tag{2}
\]
The ordering in \(\text{lem:z-blind-coarsening}\) then gives
\[
L(p)>L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_L(p)\cap\mathcal E_K=\varnothing.
\tag{3}
\]

Similarly, the blind upper dual is
\[
\min_{\alpha,\mu}\left\{\alpha+\mu^{\top}K_{\mathrm{blind}}p:
\alpha\mathbf 1+B^{\top}K_{\mathrm{blind}}^{\top}\mu\geq h_e\right\},
\tag{4}
\]
which is the restriction of the full upper dual to \(\mathcal D_U\cap\mathcal E_K\).  Hence
\[
U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)=U(p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_U(p)\cap\mathcal E_K\neq\varnothing,
\]
and the upper ordering in \(\text{lem:z-blind-coarsening}\) gives
\[
U(p)<U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda_U(p)\cap\mathcal E_K=\varnothing.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (2)--(5) also prove the advertised computable characterization: after the finite primal programs produce \(L(p)\) and \(U(p)\), each displayed intersection condition is a finite linear feasibility problem in \((\alpha,\lambda,\mu)\).

By the continuity lemma, the gap functions
\[
g_L(p)=L(p)-L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p),
\qquad
g_U(p)=U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)-U(p)
\tag{6}
\]
are continuous on \(\mathfrak O\).  Consequently
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}
=g_L^{-1}((0,\infty))\cap g_U^{-1}((0,\infty))
\tag{7}
\]
is relatively open in \(\mathfrak O\).

It remains to prove nonemptiness under \(\mathsf{Bracket}_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  Fix \(s_*\) and \(q_\ell<q_m<q_h\) supplied by \(\text{def:bracket-stratum-design}\).  Extend every row of \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\) to all additional performance values.  For \(z=0\), set the neutral outcome equal to one for every \(q\), and extend the nonincreasing \(r=1\) path by
\[
Y_{(1,q)}=
\begin{cases}
Y_{(1,q_\ell)},&q<q_m,\\
Y_{(1,q_m)},&q=q_m,\\
Y_{(1,q_h)},&q>q_m.
\end{cases}
\tag{8}
\]
For \(z=1\), set the neutral outcome equal to zero for every \(q\) and use (8) for the nondecreasing \(r=1\) path.  The extension agrees at the three distinguished values, is monotone in the required direction, and lies below the neutral value for \(z=0\) and above it for \(z=1\).  Therefore correctness, both performance orders, and neutral invariance hold at every additional \(q\).

Retain the two endpoint action bits and set every action coordinate not read by a trial arm at \(s_*\) to zero.  This includes \(A_{(1,q_m)}\): deployment uses it, but \(e\notin J_0\), and the target reads only \(Y_{(1,q_m)}\).  Legality places no cross-coordinate restriction on actions, so all thirty-two extensions remain legal.

Conversely, restrict any legal type with \(S=s_*\) to \(q_\ell,q_m,q_h\).  Its binary monotone outcome path has one of the canonical observable--target representatives in \(\text{thm:complete-32-type-refinement-certificate}\), after replacing an unread neutral constant by its displayed representative if necessary.  Its endpoint action pair is one of the four binary pairs, and all unread action coordinates may be fixed without changing the trial law or the outcome-only target.  Thus every legal type supported on \(s_*\) has the same observable--target column as one of the extended rows.  Extra performance values and off-stratum configurations create no new column in a law supported on \(s_*\).

Assign the weights \(w^{32}(\pi^{32,\circ})\) to fixed legal extensions of the thirty-two rows and zero mass to types outside \(s_*\); call the resulting mixture \(w_0\).  A trial arm \(j\) using endpoint \(d\in\{\ell,h\}\) contributes \(\rho_j\) times its conditional-cell indicator, whereas the canonical table contributes one half of that indicator.  Thus its block is the canonical endpoint block multiplied by \(2\rho_j>0\).  The bracket condition supplies at least one arm of each endpoint type.  Selecting one such block of each type and dividing by \(2\rho_j\) is a left inverse, so equality of expanded full laws is equivalent to equality of canonical full laws; the same holds after label coarsening.  Moreover, a law with zero mass outside \(s_*\) cannot be generated using a positive weight on another stratum, since every arm probability is positive and every incidence entry is nonnegative.  Duplicate or rescaled endpoint arms and other strata therefore enlarge neither relevant fiber.

The four endpoint programs at \(p_0=Bw_0\) are consequently the canonical programs at \(p^{32,\circ}\), after quotienting duplicate columns.  The exact certificate gives
\[
L(p_0)-L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p_0)=\frac{199}{800},
\qquad
U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p_0)-U(p_0)=\frac{199}{800}.
\tag{9}
\]
Thus \(p_0\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}\).

Because the finite legal class is nonempty, choose \(u\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) with \(u_t>0\) for every legal type.  For \(0<\delta<1\), set
\[
w_\delta=(1-\delta)w_0+\delta u,
\qquad
p_\delta=Bw_\delta.
\tag{10}
\]
Every coordinate of \(w_\delta\) is positive.  Aggregate weights of duplicate columns and enumerate the distinct generators as \(b_1,\ldots,b_N\), with aggregate weights \(\beta_k>0\).  On \(\{x:\mathbf 1^{\top}x=0\}\), the map \(T(x)=\sum_kx_kb_k\) surjects onto \(V=\operatorname{span}\{b_k-b_1:2\leq k\leq N\}\).  Choose a linear right inverse \(R\).  If \(V\neq\{0\}\), the finite-dimensional constant \(C=\sup_{\|d\|_2=1}\|Rd\|_\infty\) is finite, and \(\beta+Rd\) remains nonnegative whenever \(\|d\|_2<\min_k\beta_k/C\).  These weights have mass one and generate \(p_\delta+d\).  The case \(V=\{0\}\) is immediate.  Hence \(p_\delta\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O)\).

By continuity of the two gaps in (6), both remain positive for all sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), since both equal \(199/800\) at \(\delta=0\).  Therefore
\[
p_\delta\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{strict}}\cap\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O).
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (7) and (11) prove the required nonempty relatively open region.  The block-rescaling and legal-extension construction explicitly proves robustness to duplicate endpoint arms, arbitrary positive randomization probabilities, extra performance values, other strata, and off-stratum configurations.

statements.statement: Let \(X_i\), indexed by a finite or countable set, be independent centered random vectors in \(\mathbb R^d\), let \(W=\sum_iX_i\), and suppose \(\sum_i\operatorname{Var}(X_i)=I_d\).  Then, for every measurable convex set \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), \[\left|\Pr\{W\in A\}-\mathcal N(0,I_d)\{A\}\right|\leq(42d^{1/4}+16)\sum_i\mathbb E\|X_i\|_2^3.\] No conclusion for a singular total covariance is asserted.
